During this first half of the semester, my group A8 have performed exceptionally well in getting to know each other and working together with each other in order to complete any assigned tasks, as well as gather ideas for our RGM Project.

We all made sure that each and every one of us was participating equally to complete the tasks, by assigning a person with a different role each week (either Minute Taker, Chair Person or Presenter), and also by checking up on each other to see whether or not that task was completed and if they needed any help with their task.

An important factor for all of us to successfully build our relationship as a team was for us to first get-to-know each other. This was approached by creating a Team Charter during our first workshop, in which we listed down our long term goals – such as achieving professionalism within our group, maintaining a positive relationship with each other, becoming better presenters and leaders, and upholding a level of high quality of work throughout the semester as a group – as well as our personal goals that we wanted to accomplish by the end of the unit – which includes: Contributing fairly to the group work, learning new skills professional/interpersonal skills from our team members and actively learning from each other.

By listing down these goals, we were able to all have the same common purpose. This gave us a sense of direction of how we would all work together and gave us responsibilities that we needed to fulfil.

Regularly reviewing our group’s performance during our past workshops with our tutors was also a factor that lead to forming an effective team. After the presenter of our group has presented their work to the tutor room, our Minute Taker would record down the feedback given to us. Along with this feedback, the feedback given for our team reflection and minutes would also be collected and with all of this, we would look over them and discuss how we could improve for the upcoming weeks.

This technique has significantly improved our presentations later on in the semester, as we were more confident and prepared, however, we did not bring as-much significance in this technique for our Minutes. We should have focused more on improving our Minutes for each week, in order to achieve our best possible outcome.

As well as tutor’s feedback, we lacked giving each other constructive criticism. In order for us to maintain being an effective team, it is important to give each other feedback on how we performed during our workshop and during our private weekly meetings. This will allow for all of us to improve our contribution to the group, as well as improve our employability skills for the future (in the workplace environment and in other units at Macquarie University).
